name: Lying Cable Curl
description: The lying cable curl is performed face-up on a bench placed close to a low cable pulley, with both hands gripping a straight bar or EZ-bar attached to the cable. Because the lifter is horizontal, the cable pull direction creates maximum bicep tension in the stretched (extended arm) position — the opposite of standing curls which are hardest near lockout. This makes it valuable for training the bicep in its lengthened position for hypertrophy.

execution.starting_position: Place a flat bench parallel to and close to a low cable pulley. Lie face-up with the head nearest the pulley. Grasp a straight bar attached to the cable.
execution.setup_instructions: Position the bench so the cable pulls the arms toward the pulley when extended. Ensure the cable travels along the floor to the pulley smoothly.
steps: Step 1: Lie supine, arms extended toward the pulley, bar in supinated grip.
Step 2: Curl the bar toward the face by flexing the elbows.
Step 3: Hold at the peak for one second.
Step 4: Return to the extended position, feeling the stretch in the biceps.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the curl, inhale on the return.
common_mistakes: Lifting the head off the bench
Upper arms rising off the bench on the curl
safety_considerations: Keep upper arms pressed to the bench throughout
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full extension with stretch at the bottom, full curl at the top.
coaching_cues: Feel the stretch at the bottom
Upper arms stay on the bench
